cards.text: Ehud, the deliverer the LORD raised up for Israel (Judges 3:15), has died, and the Israelites AGAIN do evil in the sight of the LORD. AGAIN, friend, like hitting snooze on the same alarm. So the LORD sells them into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigns in Hazor, and his army commander is Sisera.

cards.question: Jabin has harshly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years, and they cry out to the LORD. Jabin has nine hundred chariots of ___.

cards.text: Deborah, a prophetess, is judging Israel, and the Israelites come to her for judgment under the Palm of Deborah. A TREE with her name on it, friend, and I thought my name carved on a handle was fancy.

cards.question: Deborah summons Barak son of Abinoam with a command from the LORD, the God of Israel. What does the LORD tell Barak to do?

answers.text: March to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men
Build an altar at Bethel and wait there
Send a gift of tribute to Jabin in Hazor

cards.question: The LORD's command to Barak comes with a promise. The LORD will draw out Sisera, his chariots and his troops to the River Kishon. Then what will the LORD do with Sisera?

answers.text: Send him back home to Hazor

cards.question: Barak answers Deborah. True or false: Barak says he'll go whether Deborah comes along or not.

cards.text: Deborah says, "I will certainly go with you," but she adds that this road will bring Barak no honor. That's a yes with a BUT, friend, and the but is doing all the heavy lifting.

cards.question: Deborah tells Barak the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a ___.

cards.text: So Deborah goes with Barak to Kedesh, and ten thousand men of Zebulun and Naphtali follow him. Meanwhile, Heber the Kenite has pitched his tent near Kedesh, so tuck that name in your apron pocket.

cards.question: Sisera hears that Barak has gone up Mount Tabor. What does Sisera do?

answers.text: Calls out all nine hundred iron chariots
Sends Barak a message asking for peace
Pulls his whole army back to Hazor

cards.question: Deborah tells Barak, "Arise, for this is the day that the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone before you?" True or false: Barak stays up on Mount Tabor and waits for Sisera to come to him.

cards.text: And in front of Barak, the LORD routs Sisera, his charioteers and his whole army. Nine hundred iron chariots, friend, and they don't matter ONE crumb.

cards.question: With his army falling apart, what does Sisera himself do?

answers.text: Leaves his chariot and runs on foot
Surrenders to Barak on the field
Hides in a cave with his officers

cards.text: Barak chases the chariots and the army all the way to Harosheth-hagoyim, and not a single man is left. Meanwhile Sisera, Mr. Nine Hundred Iron Chariots himself, is hoofing it on FOOT to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite.

cards.question: Why does Sisera run to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite?

answers.text: There was peace between Jabin and Heber
Jael was a sister of Sisera's mother
Heber owed Sisera a big favor

cards.text: Jael goes out to greet him: "Come in, my lord. Come in with me. Do not be afraid." So in he goes, and the man with nine hundred iron chariots ends up under a blanket.

cards.question: Sisera asks for a little water because he's thirsty, but Jael opens a container of ___.

cards.text: Sisera tells her to stand at the entrance and say no if anyone asks, "Is there a man here?" But as he lies sleeping from exhaustion, Jael takes a tent peg and a hammer and drives the peg through his temple, and he dies.

cards.question: Barak arrives, still chasing Sisera, and Jael goes out to greet him. What does she tell Barak?

answers.text: She'll show him the man he's seeking
No man came to her tent today

cards.text: On that day God subdues Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites, and their hand grows stronger and STRONGER against him until they destroy him. Twenty years under those iron chariots, friend, and the LORD flips the whole thing.
Chapter 4 told the story, and now Deborah and Barak SING it. The song opens with a call to bless the LORD when the princes take the lead and the people volunteer.

cards.question: The song calls out, "Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes!" True or false: the singer says this song is sung in praise of the kings and princes.
The song looks back to when the LORD went out from Seir and marched from the land of Edom. What does creation do?

answers.text: The earth trembles and the mountains quake
The rivers dry up and the sun stands still
The sea splits and the wind falls silent

cards.text: The song remembers the hard days: highways deserted and life in the villages over, until Deborah arose, "a mother in Israel." I go by Papa, friend, so I RESPECT that title.

cards.question: The song says war came to Israel's gates. When did it come?

answers.text: When they broke a treaty with Edom

cards.text: Deborah's heart is with the volunteers. She tells everyone, from riders on white donkeys to folks on the road, to ponder the voices of the singers at the watering places.

cards.question: True or false: the singers at the watering places recount the mighty deeds of Sisera.

cards.text: Then comes "Awake, awake, O Deborah!" and the people of the LORD come down from Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir and Zebulun. This song does NOT believe in the snooze button, friend.

cards.question: The princes of Issachar rush into the valley at Barak's heels. But the song asks Reuben why he sat among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks. In the clans of Reuben there was great ___.

cards.text: Gilead stays beyond the Jordan, the song asks Dan why he lingered by the ships, and Asher stays in his harbors. Friend, that's the group chat where everybody reads the message and NOBODY replies.

cards.question: But two tribes get a shout-out. True or false: the song says Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives.

cards.text: The kings of Canaan come and fight at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they take no plunder of silver. I bet they came expecting a payday, friend, and they went home with an EMPTY cookie box.

cards.question: The song says Sisera was up against more than Barak's ten thousand men. What else fought against Sisera?

cards.text: The River Kishon, that ANCIENT river, sweeps them away, so never underestimate something old, friend, I'm living proof. Then the hooves of horses thunder with the mad galloping of his stallions.

cards.question: In the song, the angel of the LORD says to curse Meroz. Why?

answers.text: They didn't come to help the LORD
They bowed down to the Baals

cards.text: The song turns to Jael, "most blessed of tent-dwelling women," who gave Sisera milk when he asked for water. Curds in a magnificent bowl, friend, he got the FANCY dish.
She reaches for the tent peg and the workman's hammer and strikes Sisera. The song says it again and again: at her feet he collapses, he falls, and there he lies dead.

cards.question: Far from the battle, someone peers through the lattice and asks, "Why is his chariot so long in coming?" Who is it?

cards.text: Her wisest ladies answer, and she keeps telling herself the warriors must be finding and dividing the spoil. But we know what happened in that tent, friend.

cards.question: The song closes: "So may all Your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest." After all this, the land has rest for ___ years.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker infer that the chariots are made of iron rather than gold or bronze. The blank asks for an unseen detail instead of testing a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Jael's welcome and the blanket give no basis for inferring milk instead of wine or oil. The baker can only guess at a detail that has not yet been revealed.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: No earlier card provides a basis for choosing forty years rather than eighty or seven. This blank requires the baker to guess an unheard number rather than reason out its meaning.
